findings.body: The workflow scanner recognizes only a literal `jobs:` line. Changing the deleted workflow fixture's header to `jobs: # required checks` makes it discover no removed jobs, so `old-check` and `lint` remain required after migration and block subsequent PRs. A commented header in a surviving workflow instead causes live checks to be removed. These are valid YAML workflow declarations ([GitHub syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax)). Handle ordinary YAML comments and indentation when identifying jobs, and extend the command-level regression test to cover them.

findings.body: An absolute local origin bypasses the refusal and restores `{owner}/{repo}` in both protection requests. With another GitHub remote or `GH_REPO` set, these placeholders can target an unrelated repository ([gh API contract](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api)). The production exception exists solely to accommodate command fixtures. Remove it and configure those fixtures with explicit GitHub fetch URLs and local push URLs, as the new origin-targeting test already does at tests/test_fix_forge_s_branch_protection_keeps_required.py:65–66.
findings.title: Simpler: test-only repository fallback → refuse unresolved origins

why: Forge's branch protection keeps required checks whose workflows a migration deletes, which blocks every later pull request once admins are enforced, and with two remotes and no gh default it can protect the wrong repo
